stories.headline: ‘Most likely fake’, says Telangana DGP on email threatening 26/11 like terror attack
stories.title: ‘Most likely fake’, says Telangana DGP on email threatening 26/11 like terror attack
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in title weight 84
article_sentences: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.

Hyderabad police intensified security across the city after receiving an email threatening bomb blasts at two prominent locations – Hotel Tourist Plaza in Kacheguda and Kacheguda Railway Station – and warning of a 26/11-style terror attack.
Although officials suspect the message to be a hoax, security arrangements have been tightened as a precaution.
The threat email, received on November 21, was reportedly sent by a person claiming links to the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT).
The sender allegedly threatened to target the hotel and railway station, claiming the attacks would kill at least 300 people.
Responding to the email, Telangana Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand said that the prima facie evidence pointed to the mail being fake.
He however also said that officials are following Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) regarding the issue.

The email had also threatened to replicate the November 26, 2008, Mumbai terror attacks in Hyderabad to avenge the killing of LeT operative Lateef Bhat and his associates by the Indian Army in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir.

Following the alert issued by the Special Branch, police personnel across Hyderabad were directed to strengthen security at the two locations and step up surveillance at crowded public spaces, including hotels, railway stations, bus stations, religious places and other key installations.
Anti-sabotage checks were carried out at the locations named in the email and other sensitive areas.
Police said no explosives were found during the searches.
Patrolling and visible policing have also been increased, while personnel have been instructed to watch out for suspicious individuals, unattended objects and vehicles.

stories.title: Kerala Literature Festival promises much for book lovers as it returns after pandemic

article_sentences: It has not taken the Kerala Literature Festival (KLF) long to earn a prominent place in the State’s cultural landscape.
After a three-year break, necessitated by the pandemic, the KLF is back in the physical world (it was held online in 2021).
The sixth edition will get under way on the Kozhikode beach on Thursday.
It promises plenty for the book lovers of Malabar and beyond over the next four years.

Writers such as Shehan Karunatilaka, who won the Booker Prize three months ago, Arundhati Roy, Shashi Tharoor, Nobel laureates Ada Yonath and Abhijit Banerjee, historians William Dalrymple, Yuval Noah Harari, Ramachandra Guha, Manu S. Pillai, actors Kamal Haasan, Prakash Raj, Mukesh, and Indrans are among those who will speak at sessions that will deal with a variety of topics.
Around 500 speakers, including those from countries such as the United States, UK, Spain, Israel, and New Zealand, will speak in 248 sessions, in fact.
“This is going to be the biggest edition of the KFL yet,” the festival’s chief facilitator.
Ravi Deecee told The Hindu.
“In 2020, the footfall for the festival was around three lakh.
We expect that number to go up to four or five lakh this time,” he added.
He said he was glad that the festival had evolved as something that was not just literature.
“For instance, we have been able to line up several prominent economists this time around.

stories.headline: India's ties with Russia an 'added value', can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM
stories.title: India's ties with Russia an 'added value', can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM
stories.summary: India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, share concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Netherlands sees India's continued engagement with Russia as an "added value," as it believes New Delhi can use its ties with Moscow to persuade it to end the Ukraine war, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said on Sunday.
Berendsen is on an official visit to India from November 22 to 23.
He co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday and reviewed the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership.

"We understand that India has its own history, its own role in the world and its own relations," Berendsen told PTI, responding to a question on India's strategic autonomy and its continued engagement with Moscow.

"We actually see it as an added value of our relationship with India that it has a relationship with Russia and can also use that relation to show Russia that it needs to put an end to this war and accept a ceasefire," he said.
The Russia-Ukraine war, in its fifth year, continues with intensified attacks from both sides.
Russia has stepped up strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, while US-brokered peace talks have made little progress beyond a prisoner swap.

Berendsen said India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, shared concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world.
"I think we're dealing with the same challenges: how to decrease dependencies, how to be more strategically autonomous on critical raw materials, technology and energy," he said.
"If you want to do that, you need to diversify, which means new partnerships.
I think the Netherlands, the EU and India are doing exactly that," he added.
On trade, he described the proposed India-European Union free trade agreement, expected to be signed in December, as a crucial step that could open opportunities beyond merchandise trade.

stories.headline: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal slams Congress for doubting Election Commission
stories.title: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal slams Congress for doubting Election Commission
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: DIBRUGARH: Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal criticised the Congress for repeatedly questioning the credibility of the Election Commission and democratic institutions, saying such political conduct undermines public confidence in the country's democratic framework.

Speaking at the Prabuddha Nagarik Sabha, organised by the civil society of Dibrugarh, Sonowal said political differences were a natural part of democracy, but political interests should not take precedence over the credibility and dignity of constitutional institutions.
"Every political party has a responsibility to uphold respect and confidence in the country's constitutional and democratic institutions, including the Election Commission.

Differences of opinion are natural in a democracy, but safeguarding the dignity of our democratic system and the credibility of its institutions, above narrow political interests, is a collective duty," Sonowal said.

Sarbananda Sonowal also highlighted the importance of an informed and responsible citizenry in enhancing democracy, promoting social development, and contributing to nation-building during his interactions with notable individuals from various fields.

Sonowal said India's emergence as one of the world's fastest-growing economies reflected the country's development journey under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, guided by the vision of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas.
He called for active participation and cooperation from all sections of society to accelerate the country's progress.
"Nation-building is not the responsibility of the government alone; it is a collective responsibility of every citizen.
The strength of our democracy lies in the awareness, active participation and sense of duty of its citizens.
As we move towards Amrit Kaal 2047, we must work together to build a strong, self-reliant and prosperous India," Sonowal said.

Referring to Assam's history, identity and the rights of its indigenous communities, he said protecting the state's language, culture, heritage and the interests of its people was a collective responsibility.
He described the issue of illegal foreign nationals as a significant concern for Assam and stressed the need for appropriate action in accordance with the law and constitutional provisions.

stories.headline: PT Usha gets relief in IOA election row as Delhi High Court rejects rival faction's petition
stories.title: PT Usha gets relief in IOA election row as Delhi High Court rejects rival faction's petition
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: PT Usha has cleared another hurdle in her bid for a second term as IOA president after the Delhi High Court dismissed a challenge to her inclusion in the electoral roll.
Here's why her nomination through the Ice Hockey Association became controversial.
New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has dismissed a petition challenging the inclusion of former Indian athlete PT Usha in the voter list for the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) elections.

The Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI) had nominated Usha as its representative to the IOA General Assembly after she failed to secure election under the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) category.
The petition was filed by Kunsang Namgyal, representing a rival faction of the Ice Hockey Association.
The faction questioned Usha's eligibility, arguing that she was not a member of the federation and therefore could not be nominated as its representative.
The nomination had been made by the faction led by IHAI president Gurpreet Singh Bakshi.
With the High Court dismissing the challenge, the legal obstacle to Usha submitting her nomination papers for the IOA elections has been removed.
The nomination process is scheduled to run from November 22 to 24.
Why was PT Usha's IOA voter list inclusion challenged?

The dispute centres on whether Usha could represent the Ice Hockey Association of India in the IOA General Assembly despite not being elected under the category reserved for sportspersons with outstanding achievements.
Usha had contested for a place among the four female Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit but failed to secure a position.

stories.headline: PM Modi's Gold Appeal: Foreign Exchange Savings, Gold Prices & Congress-Shastri Row
stories.title: PM Modi's Gold Appeal: Foreign Exchange Savings, Gold Prices & Congress-Shastri Row
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has credited citizens for responding to his appeal to avoid unnecessary gold purchases, as gold prices take a dip. Speaking at the National Skill Convocation in Lucknow, the PM said public cooperation could help conserve India's foreign exchange reserves amid global economic and energy uncertainties. The appeal, first made in Hyderabad in May, has also received backing from traders' bodies and Union Minister Piyush Goyal. But Modi's comparison with former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri's appeal to give up one meal a week during the 1965 war has triggered a political controversy, with Congress MP Imran Masood questioning the comparison. Did the appeal help India's economy, or has it become another political flashpoint?

stories.headline: Supreme Court says it favours only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi at air crisis hearing
stories.title: Supreme Court says it favours only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi at air crisis hearing
stories.summary: Supreme Court says it favours only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi at air crisis hearing
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court proposed phasing out heavy commercial vehicles from Delhi over five years, exploring battery-operated alternatives and border storage facilities while ensuring uninterrupted supplies of essential goods.

The Supreme Court on Monday said that it favoured restricting the entry of vehicles in Delhi to only those complying with BS-VI emission standards, saying it wanted only BS-VI vehicles to operate in the national capital, if not across the entire National Capital Region (NCR).

The observation was made by Justice Joymalya Bagchi during a hearing on the Delhi air pollution crisis, as the court examined restrictions on polluting vehicles and the difficulties faced by owners of BS-IV vehicles in obtaining Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates and fuel.
"We are clear, we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR," Justice Bagchi observed.
The remarks came after a counsel informed the court that an application had been filed concerning BS-IV vehicles, alleging that authorities had stopped conducting PUC tests for these vehicles.
This had created serious difficulties for owners, with some reportedly unable to obtain fuel, he argued.
Responding to the submission, Justice Bagchi indicated that the restrictions were aimed at ensuring that only vehicles meeting the stricter BS-VI emission standards operated in Delhi.
However, Chief Justice of India (CJI) said the court would maintain the status quo on the issue for at least one month and would not intervene immediately.
"Let there be status quo for this for at least one month.
We don't want to interfere," the CJI said.

Delhi has barred the entry of non-BS-VI petrol and diesel vehicles registered outside the national capital since November 1 as part of its Winter Action Plan and anti-pollution measures, with strict checks along the border.
During the hearing, the Bench also explored long-term measures to reduce vehicular pollution in Delhi, particularly by restricting the entry of heavy commercial vehicles.

stories.headline: New GDP Series Will Capture India's Changing Economy: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta
stories.title: New GDP Series Will Capture India's Changing Economy: RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta
stories.summary: India's economic data is getting a significant upgrade. RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta has welcomed the revised GDP, CPI and IIP series, highlighting how the new framework will better capture the structural transformation of the Indian economy. With the GDP base year updated to 2022-23 from 2011-12, the revised estimates incorporate changing consumption patterns, evolving sectoral composition and new sources of growth. Gupta highlights the use of double deflation in manufacturing and agriculture, wider service-sector data and improved measurement of investment. The new supply and use table framework also brings demand-side and supply-side nominal GDP estimates into closer alignment. She says these improvements will strengthen India's ability to analyse, forecast and explain economic growth.

stories.headline: 228 GW Solar, 135.8 GWh BESS Pipeline Raise Credit & Execution Risks: Study
stories.title: 228 GW Solar, 135.8 GWh BESS Pipeline Raise Credit & Execution Risks: Study
stories.summary: Two recent reports by India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) and CareEdge highlight widening credit divergence among domestic solar module manufacturers amid an increasing shift towards BESS manufacturing and rising operational capacity. Demand for BESS is rising as renewable energy additions outpace transmission infrastructure development. A recent ICRA report emphasises that execution is a key monitorable in building Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity amid growing storage demand and with enlarging tender pipeline. This trend is particularly acute in resource-rich states such as Rajasthan and Gujarat. This, in turn, is creating grid congestion and a growing need for storage to absorb surplus generation, shift supply to non-solar hours, and ease network constraints. India Rating and Research (IndiRa) special report, “Policy Access, Integration, and ROCE Will Drive Credit for Solar Module Manufacturers”, examines domestic manufacturing economics, ALMM-II and DCR implications, margin migration, technology and execution risks, BESS diversification, and the likely rating outlook for the sector. Emphasising on the impact on the BESS project, the research noted, a shift in Indian BESS market from tendering to execution, backed by policy support and a large tender pipeline. However, the rebound in battery prices, rupee depreciation and aggressive bids make timely battery procurement, robust LTSAs and offtake tie-ups critical for project viability. Credit Divergence & Solar Cell Import Dependence Affect the Indian Market Another key element is credit considerations, which are now emerging as an important factor requiring attention. Credit divergence across domestic solar module manufacturers is emerging in FY27, even as strong solar power demand continues, indicating widening differences in manufacturers' credit profiles. However, import dependence continues, with imported-cell modules being 3-4 US cents/W cheaper than domestic-content-requirement modules, even after basic customs duty. Consequently, the implementation of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) List-II will be central to absorbing domestic cell capacity. The divergence is unfolding against a backdrop of stable module capacity at 228 GW, which is more than three times the estimated annual requirement of 65-70 GW. This makes capacity utilisation, technology relevance, customer access, liquidity, and returns on capital more important than announced capacity alone. Solar to Push for Further Upstream Manufacturing From Modules to Cells and Ingots Ind-Ra marks the shift in Indian solar sector with the change in its margin pool from modules to cells. With margins likely to move further upstream towards ingots and wafers as backward integration gathers pace, its expected to favour well-capitalised integrated manufacturers. However, substantially higher capex, technology, commissioning, power, and refinancing risks will increase rating sensitivity. Therefore, the winners according to the report would be those who can provider low-debt module manufacturers with strong channels and high asset turns. This may remain viable at lower margins, while leveraged greenfield projects and standalone assemblers dependent on spot cells will be more exposed as domestic cell spreads normalise. “Policy access and integration will increasingly determine market position, but neither guarantees stronger credit quality. As manufacturers move upstream, the ability to preserve return on capital, manage technology transitions, and fund expansion without weakening liquidity will separate sustainable business models from capacity-led growth,” says Bhanu Patni, Director, Corporate Ratings, Ind-Ra. BESS Pack Costs Remain Central to Assessment At a battery pack cost of USD 70/kWh, a cumulative DSCR of 1.17-1.27 times is expected at tariffs of Rs. 2.60-2.80 lakh/MW/month. Competitive procurement and protection against cost escalation remain central to the assessment. Operational BESS capacity is also rising, signalling progress from tendering to deployment. Policy support, including the Government of India’s VGF schemes announced in 2023, 2025, and 2026, covering 135.8 GWh, provides a significant source of capital support. Battery procurement costs and currency movements remain critical to the viability of aggressively bid projects. ICRA’s sensitivity analysis highlights limited coverage headroom at lower capacity tariffs. Merchant BESS Viability: Arbitrage Margins Need Adequate Utilisation Sustained arbitrage margins and adequate utilisation are critical to merchant BESS viability. ICRA’s analysis indicates a cumulative DSCR of 1.35-1.52 times at a charging cost of Rs. 2/unit and discharge realisation of Rs. 6.0-6.5/unit, under the stated assumptions. Narrowing peak-off-peak spreads, fewer viable trading cycles, lower efficiency, and availability shortfalls remain key risks to cash flows and debt coverage, necessitating adequate liquidity buffers. Lower upfront funding and supplier guarantees do not eliminate future costs and operating risks. The report reccomends project assessments to take into account eventual duty payments under Manufacturing and Other Operations in Warehouse Regulations ( MOOWR) and check whether supplier guarantees adequately cover commitments to the power buyer. Costs not covered by the supplier, including performance penalties, additional batteries, and post-warranty maintenance, remain important risks for the developer.

Credit divergence across domestic solar module manufacturers is emerging in FY27, even as strong solar power demand continues, indicating widening differences in manufacturers' credit profiles.
However, import dependence continues, with imported-cell modules being 3-4 US cents/W cheaper than domestic-content-requirement modules, even after basic customs duty.
Consequently, the implementation of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) List-II will be central to absorbing domestic cell capacity.
The divergence is unfolding against a backdrop of stable module capacity at 228 GW, which is more than three times the estimated annual requirement of 65-70 GW.
This makes capacity utilisation, technology relevance, customer access, liquidity, and returns on capital more important than announced capacity alone.
Solar to Push for Further Upstream Manufacturing From Modules to Cells and Ingots Ind-Ra marks the shift in Indian solar sector with the change in its margin pool from modules to cells.
However, substantially higher capex, technology, commissioning, power, and refinancing risks will increase rating sensitivity.
Therefore, the winners according to the report would be those who can provider low-debt module manufacturers with strong channels and high asset turns.
This may remain viable at lower margins, while leveraged greenfield projects and standalone assemblers dependent on spot cells will be more exposed as domestic cell spreads normalise.
“Policy access and integration will increasingly determine market position, but neither guarantees stronger credit quality.

As manufacturers move upstream, the ability to preserve return on capital, manage technology transitions, and fund expansion without weakening liquidity will separate sustainable business models from capacity-led growth,” says Bhanu Patni, Director, Corporate Ratings, Ind-Ra.
BESS Pack Costs Remain Central to Assessment.
At a battery pack cost of USD 70/kWh, a cumulative DSCR of 1.17-1.27 times is expected at tariffs of Rs.
2.60-2.80 lakh/MW/month.
Competitive procurement and protection against cost escalation remain central to the assessment.
Operational BESS capacity is also rising, signalling progress from tendering to deployment.
Policy support, including the Government of India’s VGF schemes announced in 2023, 2025, and 2026, covering 135.8 GWh, provides a significant source of capital support.
Battery procurement costs and currency movements remain critical to the viability of aggressively bid projects.
ICRA’s sensitivity analysis highlights limited coverage headroom at lower capacity tariffs.
Merchant BESS Viability: Arbitrage Margins Need Adequate Utilisation Sustained arbitrage margins and adequate utilisation are critical to merchant BESS viability.
ICRA’s analysis indicates a cumulative DSCR of 1.35-1.52 times at a charging cost of Rs.
2/unit and discharge realisation of Rs.
6.0-6.5/unit, under the stated assumptions.
Narrowing peak-off-peak spreads, fewer viable trading cycles, lower efficiency, and availability shortfalls remain key risks to cash flows and debt coverage, necessitating adequate liquidity buffers.
Lower upfront funding and supplier guarantees do not eliminate future costs and operating risks.

The report reccomends project assessments to take into account eventual duty payments under Manufacturing and Other Operations in Warehouse Regulations ( MOOWR) and check whether supplier guarantees adequately cover commitments to the power buyer.
Costs not covered by the supplier, including performance penalties, additional batteries, and post-warranty maintenance, remain important risks for the developer.

stories.headline: Right to correct electoral roll entry is personal, can't pursue in PIL: SC
stories.title: Right to correct electoral roll entry is personal, can't pursue in PIL: SC
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a PIL seeking corrections to municipal electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh over discrepancies in house numbers. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it was not inclined to entertain the plea. "The right to seek correction of an electoral-roll entry is personal to the individual voter and cannot ordinarily be pursued collectively through a PIL. The municipal electoral rolls are governed by their own rules, and individual voters can approach the competent election authorities for corrections," Justice Bagchi orally observed. The petitioner had argued that house numbers had changed, representations remained unaddressed and municipal electoral rolls should be aligned with those used for parliamentary and Assembly elections.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks petitioner to move Allahabad High Court over ‘demolition’ of 100-year-old mosque at Saharanpur
stories.summary: Declining to directly examine the allegations, the Supreme Court asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
event term: 'supreme court judgment' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) declined to entertain a plea alleging that the demolition of a 100-year-old mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur district violated the demolition guidelines laid down by it in a landmark 2024 judgment on the use of bulldozers.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was hearing a plea filed by Imran Ahmad against Uttar Pradesh Chief Secretary Shashi Prakash Goyal, alleging non-compliance with the apex court's directions.

Declining to undertake a direct examination of the allegations, the Bench asked the petitioner to approach the jurisdictional High Court, saying that every alleged violation of a Supreme Court judgment cannot be brought directly before the apex court.
"Every order violating a Supreme Court judgment cannot come back to the Supreme Court itself.
You have to go to the respective high court," CJI said.

The Bench said determining whether the demolition guidelines had been violated would require an examination of the specific facts and circumstances surrounding the alleged demolition, a task more appropriately undertaken by the jurisdictional High Court.
"We have laid down the principles, but then wherever these principles have been violated, in what factual context and background?
Please go to the concerned high court, establish your case on facts, and if the high court doesn't grant you necessary relief, then come to us," the CJI said.
The Bench further clarified that it could not undertake a factual inquiry into the allegations in the contempt proceedings.
However, the Bench made it clear that if the High Court, upon examining the matter, finds that the Supreme Court's directions have been violated, appropriate consequences would follow.
The petitioner was asked to approach the jurisdictional High Court and seek appropriate relief.
The Bench said that the matter be decided expeditiously.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks response of Centre, ECI on PIL for reforms in anti-defection law
stories.summary: The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) sought responses from the Centre, the Election Commission of India and the Law Commission on a PIL seeking comprehensive reforms in the anti-defection framework.
The PIL raised concerns over alleged misuse of resignations by elected representatives to circumvent disqualification proceedings and influence the survival of elected governments.

Besides the Election Commission and the law panel, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also issued notices to the Ministries of Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs on the PIL filed by A. Sethu.

The PIL, filed through lawyers R. Satish Kumar and Jatin, sought directions to prevent misuse of “strategic resignations” by MPs and lawmakers from legislative assemblies to evade discipline of the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution.

It also sought directions to “(ii) secure time-bound, reasoned and transparent adjudication of resignations and disqualification proceedings; (iii) secure institutional review of the Speaker-centred adjudicatory mechanism; and (iv) reaffirm that in a hung Legislative Assembly, majority to form the Government must be tested only on the floor of a duly constituted House after Members are sworn under Article 188, and not through extra-parliamentary letters of support or demonstrations.”
The plea said that legislators facing, or anticipating, disqualification proceedings frequently resort to strategic resignations before the Speaker or Chairman can decide the cases on merit.

The plea said such resignations can be used to facilitate political realignments, alter the numerical strength of legislative assemblies and potentially enable elected representatives to evade the consequences contemplated under the anti-defection law.

“Declare and direct that a resignation tendered by a Member of Parliament or a Member of a State Legislative Assembly, at a stage when disqualification proceedings under the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution are pending or reasonably imminent against such member, shall not ipso facto terminate or render infructuous such disqualification proceedings, and that the Speaker/Chairman shall record a reasoned order, based on objective material, on both the voluntariness and genuineness of the resignation and on the disqualification petition,” the plea said.

The plea sought direction to Speakers and Chairpersons to examine the voluntariness and genuineness of resignations on the basis of objective material and pass reasoned orders, while ensuring that pending disqualification proceedings are independently adjudicated.

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) that sought corrections to municipal electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh over alleged discrepancies in house numbers.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana declined to entertain the plea.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that the right to seek correction of an electoral-roll entry is personal to the individual voter and cannot ordinarily be pursued collectively through a PIL.
“You are moving this petition as a public interest litigation.
The right to correct an electoral roll is personal.
In your municipal list also, there will be certain rules.
Let the individuals approach.
But on a collective basis, it can only be when it is done across the State.
Voters can take it up.
Individual voters can come to us,” Justice Bagchi said.
The Court noted that municipal electoral rolls are governed by their own set of rules and that individual voters can approach the competent election authorities for necessary corrections.

The petitioner had contended that house numbers had changed in several areas, that representations made in this regard remained unaddressed, and that municipal electoral rolls should be aligned with those prepared for parliamentary and assembly elections.

stories.headline: Kashmir must heed Nepal's warning, protect fragile Himalayas: Mirwaiz on Sheshnag lake excavator video
stories.title: Kashmir must heed Nepal's warning, protect fragile Himalayas: Mirwaiz on Sheshnag lake excavator video
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 23: Mirwaiz-e-Kashmir Dr Moulvi Mohammad Umar Farooq on Monday expressed concern over reports of heavy machinery being used near Sheshnag Lake in the glacial zone of Pahalgam, questioning the ecological impact of construction activities in the fragile Himalayan region. In a post on X, Mirwaiz said visuals and reports of heavy machinery operating near the lake were disturbing and had raised serious concerns among people about the environmental impact of such activities. He said retreating glaciers and recent devastating glacier-related floods in neighbouring Nepal were reminders of the growing vulnerability of the Himalayan region. Mirwaiz said Kashmir had always warmly welcomed pilgrims undertaking the Amarnath Yatra and that improving facilities for them was not an issue, but stressed that such development should not come at the cost of the fragile ecosystem. "Those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such 'developmental projects'!" he said. Calling for an immediate halt to the reported activities, Mirwaiz said the mountains, glaciers and water bodies needed protection for present and future generations. "Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection not plunder, for now and for the future generations. So this must be immediately stopped," he said. The statement comes amid concerns raised by political leaders over purported visuals circulating on social media that allegedly show heavy machinery being used near Sheshnag Lake for construction work along the Amarnath Yatra route.

stories.headline: India to include data as an asset in GDP calculations in next base revision: MoSPI
stories.title: India to include data as an asset in GDP calculations in next base revision: MoSPI
stories.summary: The proposed changes are part of a broader statistical overhaul covering national accounts, household income measurement and district-level economic estimates
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Government ministries across the board are focusing on ensuring greater transparency and wider availability of data, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) Secretary Saurabh Garg said on Monday, outlining upcoming structural shifts in how India measures its economy.

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), and Index of Industrial Production (IIP), organised in collaboration with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Garg stated that central departments are actively working to make granular information accessible to the public.
“I think both the Ministry of Panchayati Raj and the Ministry of Housing are working on this.
You might be aware there’s already a Panchayat Advancement Index which is published annually and which has a lot of granular information of the status of each Panchayat,” Garg noted.
“Similarly, the Ministry of Housing also has developed a portal in which a lot of these accounts are being published.
So I think all ministries are focusing on this work to ensure that there is greater transparency and availability of data,” he added.
A key pillar of the ministry’s upcoming statistical overhaul involves integrating digital information directly into national accounting.

Referring to the digital transformation sparked by the Digital India initiative in 2015, Garg explained that India is now a data-rich nation and will soon reflect this in its headline economic metrics.

“The fact that the system of national accounts 2025 focuses on data as an asset is something the mechanics, the details are being worked out and when the next base revision is done, we’ll have data as an asset as an integral part of calculation of the GDP,” the Secretary said.
Alongside GDP revisions, MoSPI is nearing the final stretch of its nationwide household income survey, which began in April this year.
Garg reported that the fieldwork is nearly complete, with completion targeted for March.
“The kind of response that we are getting from households has been extremely encouraging.
